name: Hechtsee
kurzbeschreibung: The Hechtsee near Kufstein is the region's deepest lake at 57 m: idyllic forest lake at 542 m, Strandbad Seearena, 2.8 km circular trail, and legendary lore.
oeffnungszeiten: Rundweg 24/7 frei zugänglich; Strandbad Mai–Sep täglich 09:00–19:00/20:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Hechtsee lies nestled in dense mixed forests at the foot of the Thierberg ridge, roughly three kilometres north of the fortress town of Kufstein in the Tyrolean Unterinntal. Situated at an elevation of 542 metres above sea level, the lake spans a water surface area of around 0.28 square kilometres. With a maximum water depth of 57 metres, the Hechtsee is by far the deepest bathing lake in the entire Kufstein region. As a protected local recreation area, it enchants residents and vacationers alike with premium water quality, idyllic shoreline promenades, and postcard-perfect views of the craggy peaks of the Kaisergebirge.

Nature, Legends & Strandbad

Geologically, the Hechtsee originated during the last Ice Age, when the massive Inntal glacier gouged a deep tectonic basin into the bedrock. A distinctive feature of the lake is its meromictic stratification: the bottom water below about 20 metres does not circulate with the oxygen-rich surface layer, making the lake exceptionally fascinating for limnologists. Around the lake weaves the romantic Tyrolean legend of the Nixe Hechta, a benevolent water fairy said to watch over the lake's depths. On the eastern shore lies the traditional Strandbad Seearena Hechtsee: an expansive, well-kept sunbathing lawn with shady trees, modern bathing piers, a children's pool, a beach volleyball court, and culinary establishments. In midsummer, the lake surface warms to a pleasant 23 to 25 °C. A highlight for leisurely walkers is the 2.8-kilometre Hechtsee-Rundweg: the nearly level shoreline promenade leads completely around the lake and offers, from the northern shore, a world-famous photo motif of the lake against the backdrop of the Wilder Kaiser.

Visit & Getting There

The circular lake trail and the surrounding forest grounds are freely accessible free of charge year-round. The Strandbad Seearena is open during the bathing season from May to September daily from 09:00 to 19:00 (in high summer during good swimming weather until 20:00); outside the swimming season, the beach lido grounds can also be accessed freely. Strandbad admission fees (as of the 2025/2026 season): day ticket for adults €6.50 (from 12:00 €5.00, from 16:00 €3.00), children aged 6 to 15 €3.00, seniors €5.00. Travel by car: from Kufstein on the B171 or L211 towards Thiersee, well-signposted turnoff to the large visitor car park at the Hechtsee (pay parking). By public transport: in the summer months, the Hechtsee-Shuttlebus operated by Stadtwerke Kufstein runs several times daily from Kufstein railway station directly to the lake; alternatively, an attractive hiking trail (approx. 45 minutes) leads up from Kufstein through the woods to the lake.

Tips

The 2.8 km Hechtsee circular trail is flat almost throughout, lined with fine gravel, and ideally suited for walks with strollers and wheelchairs. Those seeking a longer trek can embark on the Vier-Seen-Wanderung, connecting the Hechtsee with the nearby smaller forest lakes Egelsee, Längsee, and Pfrillsee. Stop at the Seearena lakeside restaurant and enjoy freshly caught fish out on the lake terrace.
